editorial:
Till the Clouds Roll By is MGM's 1946 Technicolor musical built around the songs of Jerome Kern, released December 5, 1946. A creator would want it for its period musical numbers and its place in the studio's Technicolor catalog.

The rights trap is that no renewal was confirmed or ruled out. A Catalog of Copyright Entries check of the 1974 and 1975 motion-picture volumes found no entry, but that check was partial. No Copyright Office record search was completed. The Internet Archive item page shows a Public Domain Mark 1.0, but that is only the uploader's label. Studio-owned films from this period were often renewed, so treat the print as unresolved until the records are checked directly. Kern's songs are separate compositions with their own terms.
faq: Is Till the Clouds Roll By in the public domain?

Not established. A partial check of the 1974 and 1975 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes found no renewal, and no Copyright Office record search was completed. The Internet Archive item page shows a Public Domain Mark 1.0, but that is the uploader's label, so do not rely on it.
Can I use the songs from the film?
Not safely without checking. The songs are separate compositions with their own copyright terms, and those were not individually verified.
